senses.gloss: (b. h. צָוַח)to cry, shout; to complain.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 14b:9">Keth. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>ממזר וצוֹוֵחַ</he> one that is called a bastard and brings complaint, opp. <he>שותק</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 24b:7">B. Mets. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>והלא עומד וצווֵֹחַ</he> but does he (the loser) not stand up and cry (which shows that he has not given up the hope of recovery)? <he>נעשה כצווח על וכ׳</he> it is like one crying over his house that has fallen in &c.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 138a:7">B. Bath. 138ᵃ</cite> <he>בצָ׳ מעיקרא</he> (or <he>בצוֵֹחַ</he>), <he>בצָ׳ מעיקרו</he> when he cried out (refused the gift) at the start (when it was offered to him).

<cite ref="Sotah 42b:1">Sot. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>צוְֹחִין וכ׳</he> (better <cite ref="R00152"><he>צווְֹ׳</he></cite>) they (the gentile soldiers) shout (before they attack) and stamp; <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 192:3">Sifré Deut. 192</cite> <he>צווְֹחִים</he>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: same. Y. M. Kat. III, 82ᵈ top (ref. to דֹּם, Ez. XXIV, 17) מכן שצריך לְצַוֵּוחַ (or לִצְו̇ Kal) from here we learn that ordinarily a mourner must cry out (lament). Bab.
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 24b">M. Kat. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>מְצַוְּוחִין</he> Ms. M. (v. <cite ref="R00130"><he>צָהַב</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 6:14">Tosef. Sabb. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 7:14">VII</cite>), 14 <he>המְצַוַּוחַת לתנור וכ׳</he> a woman that shouts at the stove that the bread may not fall apart (a superstitious practice).
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 20:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XX</cite> <he>מְצוַּחַת</he>; a. fr.

<cite ref="Shabbat 67b">Sabb. 67ᵇ</cite> … <he>המשתקת והמַצָוַוחַת לגריסין</he> who tells people around her to be silent, when lentils are cooked, or to shout, when grits are cooked (a superstitious practice; Tosef. l. c. 15 <he>והמציצת</he>, v. <cite ref="R00430"><he>צָיַץ</he></cite>).
